description: Heavy rainfall is causing rapid flooding in a residential area. Interpret warnings correctly, evacuate at the right time, and choose safe routes.
objectives: Decide when to evacuate rather than wait
Choose safe routes and avoid floodwater
Protect essential documents and assist vulnerable people

steps.title: The First Warning
steps.narrative: Local authorities issue a flood watch for your area after continuous heavy rainfall. Water is not yet visible on your street. What do you do?

options.text: Start preparing now — pack an emergency kit and important documents
Wait until water is actually visible before doing anything
options.mistake: Waiting for visible water wastes valuable preparation time — a watch means conditions are favorable for flooding.

options.text: Ignore it, warnings are usually exaggerated
options.mistake: Dismissing an official warning is one of the most common causes of preventable flood casualties.

steps.title: Water Rises
steps.narrative: Water is now visible on the street and rising quickly. An evacuation advisory is issued for low-lying areas, which includes your home.

options.text: Evacuate now, on foot or by vehicle, following the advisory
Wait to see if the water keeps rising before deciding
options.mistake: Delaying evacuation after an advisory is issued for your area sharply increases risk as routes can become impassable.

steps.title: Choosing a Route
steps.narrative: Your usual route out is now partially underwater. A message says a stretch of the main road is flooded. What do you do?

options.text: Take the alternate, higher-ground route even though it's longer
Drive through the flooded road since your car looks high enough
options.mistake: Just 30 cm of moving water can sweep away most vehicles — never drive through flooded roads.

options.text: Walk through the flooded section instead
options.mistake: Floodwater can hide strong currents, open drains, and debris — walking through it is dangerous.

steps.title: A Vulnerable Neighbour
steps.narrative: On your way, you pass an elderly neighbour who hasn't evacuated and has no transport.

options.text: Help them evacuate safely if you can, or alert emergency responders to their location
Continue on your own way — it's not your responsibility
options.mistake: Assisting vulnerable people when it is safe to do so, or alerting responders, is a core part of community disaster response.

steps.title: Resource Check
steps.narrative: You reach a temporary shelter. Supplies are limited. You have your emergency kit with you.

options.text: Register with shelter staff and share your situation and needs clearly
Keep to yourself and don't tell anyone you're there
options.mistake: Not registering at a shelter makes it harder for responders to track who is safe and who needs help.

steps.title: After the Peak
steps.narrative: Reports say the water level is dropping in your neighbourhood. Should you return home immediately?

options.text: Wait for an official all-clear before returning; floodwater can hide hazards afterward
Go back immediately since the water looks lower now
options.mistake: Returning before an official all-clear risks contact with contaminated water, damaged electrical systems, or structural damage.
